issues: Postprandial and late-day glucose elevation (hourly averages of 153 to 162 mg/dL from 15:00 to 18:00 local time).
Overnight and early morning hypoglycemia risk (time below 70 mg/dL at 5.1% with glucose minimums dipping into the 40s mg/dL).
Absence of manual carbohydrate entries in the treatment summary, placing full reliance on UAM and closed-loop automation.
summary: Analysis of 14 days of Nightscout telemetry and AAPS profile data shows an overall time-in-range of 86.0%, with stable glucose variability (CV 32.6%). However, notable time below range (5.1%) occurs overnight, and postprandial upward drift is observed in the afternoon hours. The user relies heavily on closed-loop automation (SMB and UAM enabled) and GLP-1 therapy (1.25mg) to manage glucose without logging formal meal carbohydrates.
education: Maintaining SMB and UAM active helps compensate for unannounced meal absorption, but logging approximate meal carbohydrates improves IOB and COB prediction accuracy.
Dynamic ISF and sensitivity ratios adapt insulin delivery in real-time, reducing the need for aggressive static profile changes.
strengths: High data completeness with 98.7% CGM coverage over 14 days.
Responsive closed-loop automation using oref1 microbolusing and dynamic sensitivity.
safety_notes: TuneMyBG prepares data for review only and does not provide medical advice.
This is decision-support content only. The user must independently verify every proposed change, make changes one at a time, and monitor glucose closely.

analysis_steps.evidence: 3,995 CGM entries spanning 14 days with 98.7% coverage, 10 gaps (largest 65 minutes), and robust telemetry.
analysis_steps.findings: Data quality is good and supports thorough evaluation.
analysis_steps.data_gaps: Minor gaps do not hinder trend analysis.

analysis_steps.evidence: TIR 86.0%, TAR 8.9%, TBR 5.1%, CV 32.6%, with recorded glucose extremes in the 40s and 50s mg/dL.
analysis_steps.findings: Hypoglycemia risk during overnight/early morning hours acts as a strict constraint against aggressive insulin increases.
analysis_steps.data_gaps: Lack of explicit carb entries complicates postprandial vs basal separation.

analysis_steps.evidence: Local hourly glucose shows overnight dipping (00:00-01:00 averages 90-93 mg/dL with 11-18% below range) and afternoon elevations (15:00-18:00 averages 153-162 mg/dL).
analysis_steps.findings: Early morning basal may be slightly too strong, while afternoon hours show upward drift from uncaptured meal impact.
analysis_steps.data_gaps: Absence of direct carb tracking limits pure basal drift isolation.

analysis_steps.evidence: Flat ISF of 56 mg/dL/U, CR segments 10.5-13.3 g/U, DIA 10 hours, and active dynamic ISF (70%).
analysis_steps.findings: Closed-loop microbolusing and dynamic sensitivity heavily influence therapy response windows.
analysis_steps.data_gaps: Separation of pure ISF response is confounded by simultaneous automated loop interventions.

analysis_steps.evidence: smb_enabled=true, uam_enabled=true, smb_always_enabled=true, with frequent UAM-triggered microboluses in loop logs.
analysis_steps.findings: Configuration supports unannounced meal management effectively given the lack of logged carbs.
analysis_steps.data_gaps: Reliance on rate-of-change detection without carb entry can occasionally cause over-delivery.

analysis_steps.evidence: autosens_enabled=false, dynamic_sensitivity_enabled=true (70%), max_basal=12 U/h, max_iob=25 U.
analysis_steps.findings: Dynamic ISF successfully adapts sensitivity without requiring Autosens or profile changes.

analysis_steps.evidence: carb_entries: 0, regular GLP-1 administration (1.25mg) noted in representative events.
analysis_steps.findings: Meals are managed via closed-loop automation and GLP-1 delayed absorption without manual carb boluses.
analysis_steps.data_gaps: Absence of explicit meal bolus timing data.

analysis_steps.evidence: carb_treatment_entries empty, min_5m_carbimpact=8 mg/dL/5 min, meal_max_absorption_hours=7 h.
analysis_steps.findings: E-carbs are not utilized; the 7-hour absorption window adequately supports GLP-1 delayed gastric emptying.
analysis_steps.data_gaps: No e-carb or extended carb entries in telemetry.

analysis_steps.evidence: Synthesized findings from data quality, safety overview, basal/targets, profile settings, AAPS automation, and meal strategies.
analysis_steps.findings: Current settings are overall effective and safe under closed-loop control. Withhold profile changes pending targeted verification of meal logging and monitoring of overnight lows.
analysis_steps.data_gaps: Lack of manual carb entries limits precision of automated COB predictions.

recommendations.title: Monitor Overnight Basal and Hypoglycemia
recommendations.description: Overnight glucose data shows time below range reaching up to 18.5% at 01:00 local time. Verify overnight basal delivery before making any adjustments.

suggested_change.rationale: Withhold changes until overnight low patterns are further monitored with manual verification.

recommendations.title: Evaluate Carbohydrate Logging
recommendations.description: With zero recorded carb entries, AAPS relies entirely on UAM. Logging approximate carbs for key meals can improve IOB and COB prediction accuracy.

suggested_change.rationale: Observe impact of optional carb logging on afternoon postprandial peaks.

profile_recommendation.rationale: Overall time-in-range is strong at 86.0%, and closed-loop automation with Dynamic ISF effectively manages variability. Observed overnight lows and afternoon elevations warrant close monitoring rather than immediate parameter changes.
profile_recommendation.next_check: Monitor overnight glucose trends and evaluate whether logging approximate meal carbohydrates reduces afternoon postprandial elevations.
profile_recommendation.recommendation: Keep current profile settings and observe overnight stability and afternoon glucose patterns closely.

meal_strategy_summary.suggestion: Maintain closed-loop automation (SMB enabled, UAM enabled with a 7-hour absorption window) to manage unannounced meals and GLP-1 delayed absorption. Consider logging approximate carbohydrate amounts for key meals to improve IOB and COB prediction accuracy.
meal_strategy_summary.rationale: The user relies entirely on UAM and SMB without manual carb entries, supported by GLP-1 therapy (1.25mg) which flattens and delays postprandial peaks.
meal_strategy_summary.next_observation: Log explicit carbohydrate entries for a subset of meals over a 3-day test period to evaluate whether COB-guided dosing reduces afternoon postprandial elevations without increasing overnight hypoglycemia.
